clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock ended Week 82 at 7:40 p.m. public time, unchanged from the close of Week 81, with an internal shift of only one-tenth of a minute backward. This was among the smallest measured movements recorded, reflecting a week in which damage and resistance nearly canceled each other out rather than a week of genuine stability.

grand_total_points.note: Net movement was nearly flat, reflecting a near-cancellation between substantial negative pressure and partial, real resistance.

delta_summary.moral_floor: The floor held only because opposing forces happened to balance, not because the underlying structure grew more secure.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: Week 82 saw the clock barely move despite intense underlying activity: a politicized Justice Department, unprecedented presidential self-enrichment, and open defiance of a federal court order pushed backward, while scattered judicial rulings and a stalled defense budget held the line. long_synopsis: Week 82 opened with the confirmation of Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer, as Attorney General, and closed with a Kennedy Center board defying a federal court order. In between, the Justice Department revived dismissed prosecutions, DHS ran undercover surveillance against protest groups, and ICE moved to procure electric-shock gloves. Trump's family generated roughly $2.2 billion in personal revenue through crypto ventures, a paid early-access subscription for presidential posts, and diverted funds for White House renovations. Courts pushed back in places, dismissing a lawsuit against Harvard and blocking a $400 million ballroom project, while the Senate stalled a defense budget. Officials disputed their own economic data as job losses mounted. The clock moved only one-tenth of a minute backward, the public hour held at 7:40 p.m., but the architecture beneath it kept shifting.
short_synopsis: A politicized Attorney General, a president's swelling private fortune, and defiance of a federal court order nearly balanced against scattered judicial and legislative resistance. The clock barely moved, but the week's damage and pushback masked a structure growing less secure underneath.
